item.title: This is predatory abuse, not love
item.description:
I stumbled upon this gem today. I’m worried about the women out there that have been conditioned to believe that this sort of man is someone whose opinion is respectable. We still live in a world where virginity is often interchangeable with worth. Things like “body count” are used as trophies for men, and a mark of shame for women. Some people might view a man like this as someone with self-respect who only picks up women of value. This is not a respectable man with decent standards. This is a predatory monster whose standards are women he can exploit. I’ll show you the full post.
The more I read, the worse it got.
In this one, I’ve underlined the most alarming parts. No one should EVER say that protection is a personal failure. No one should EVER say that submission is the definition of a good partner because what they’re ACTUALLY saying is that they want to subjugate you. These are the words of an abuser. These are the words of someone who is appraising your value by how much sexual control they can exert over you. This is not someone who will ever truly love you.
Like I said, this is a man who wants to take you in as a possession and plunder you for his own satisfaction. You are a human being with your own thoughts, feelings, dreams, and worth that is just as important as your partner’s. You do not deserve to be appraised by your boundaries.
Love is not a toy box where you can take what you want, play with it, and put it away until you want to play with it again - or leave it on the floor for someone else to trip on. You give, you take, and then you give again. It’s a symbiotic relationship, not a parasitic one. Do not let anyone define who you are as a person, but especially a man like this. There is love out there that is real, but this is not an example of it.

item.title: Trans Dating - Lost and Found
item.description: I have been posting these cause you all seem to love them (some of you too much, my DMs here on imgur have blow up since starting this series...) Anyway, context before the comments inevitably do what they have on these posts: These videos start where the actual conversation started. The messages you see at the beginning are the first DMs these guys sent me... I’m not cutting out some earlier conversation that makes them make more sense. My dating profile also explicitly says that I’m trans and pre-op. They know. I promise, you do not need to accuse me of being the stereotype... I generally only turn conversations into videos when they eventually get weird, hostile, or the guy turns on me. Often I leave that part out because the interaction is funnier without it, or because I’d rather end on the joke than the ugliness. Obligatory wholesome disclaimer: All of the ad revenue from my YouTube channel goes to trans charities. So if you watch these idiots be idiots over there, they accidentally help trans people. Which remains one of my favorite parts of this entire project. I’ve also genuinely loved posting these because it’s given me another way to connect with other trans folks over the shared absurdity of trying to date while trans. My Channel: https://youtube.com/shorts/IJcLPqjomRw

The Postal Service issued that rule on Friday, three days before the justices called the case premature. Wednesday morning, 10 weeks before Election Day, the states returned to court with the receipts. I've emailed 8,822 stories over 573 straight nights, free and without ads. *Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley told Fox News that the country has to prioritize a compromise between privacy and safety. *He compared calls for an outright ban to banning vehicles, pointing to drunk driving and seatbelt laws as the better model. *Langley's remarks followed a Washington Post investigation that found police departments were not auditing how officers used the cameras.
A Washington Post investigation published on August 19 found at least 69 police officials accused, charged or convicted of misusing Flock or similar plate readers. In at least 15 of those cases, the person who spotted it first was outside the department: a victim, an activist or a journalist. Reporters then identified three more officers by analyzing public search logs. One in Indianapolis had run 3,759 searches over ten months on vehicles used by his wife and two acquaintances, roughly twelve a day. All three departments said they did not regularly audit officer searches, and two of the officers have since been disciplined.
